verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this finding are published, and the join between them is weaker than it looks. The $117,306,232 firm-fixed-price P550 order is DoD daily-contracts wire copy: ExecutiveBiz dates the award 2026-06-03 and ClearanceJobs carried it 2026-06-04, and AeroVironment itself press-released it on 2026-07-20 with heavy re-syndication on 07-21/07-22. That award was therefore public roughly four weeks BEFORE the 2026-06-29 Q4 FY26 call at which management issued FY27 revenue guidance of $2.125-2.225B, and public again before the fiscal quarter closed on 2026-08-01. Every sell-side model built after 06-29 had the award in hand. The other half -- $306.4M product-sales consensus, -2.3% YoY -- is not a private calculation either; it is the Zacks key-metrics consensus syndicated on Yahoo Finance on 2026-09-03, six days before the print. So the only unpublished element is the inference that the two are incompatible, and that inference rests on reading a DoD 'estimated completion date' of 2026-07-23 as a revenue-recognition schedule. It is not one: it is the period-of-performance end on a BOA call order whose place of performance was explicitly 'to be determined with individual orders', and at least one secondary rendering of the same announcement gives work beginning 2026-08-03 and completing 2026-10-31, which would put the entire program in Q2 FY27 and outside this print. The more parsimonious explanation for a product line modelled down 2.3% with a known $117M order inside it is that analysts know the deliveries are not all Q1 revenue, or that Switchblade/JUMP-20 volumes are declining underneath. Finally, the baseline is already leaning this way: a 25-delta skew of -15.51 means calls are bid over puts into the print, i.e. the option market is explicitly paying for the upside surprise this finding predicts.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Carries the verbatim DoD announcement of the $117,306,232 FFP order for 82 P550 UAS, Army Contracting Command Redstone Arsenal, with an estimated completion date of 2026-07-23.
Dates the award itself to 2026-06-03 and notes ten proposals received and work locations determined with individual orders.
AeroVironment's own press release announcing the $117.3M initial full-rate P550 production award -- issued before the fiscal quarter closed 2026-08-01.
Publishes the exact consensus the finding uses -- product sales $306.40M (-2.3% YoY), contract services $150.43M, total $474.57M, EPS $0.32.
Pre-print consensus of $459.9M revenue and $0.30 EPS, with revenue estimates described as stable and the concern located in margins rather than the top line.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: This is a bullish claim and it is agreeing with the option market, not contradicting it. The 25-delta skew is -15.51 vol points -- calls richer than puts, the baseline's own 'upside paid' lean -- on a name 26.7% lower over twenty sessions and 65% off its 52-week high. That is precisely the configuration of a market that has sold the shares down on the SCAR/legal story but is paying for an upside catalyst at the print. Front-expiry ATM IV of 168.8% with an 11.87% implied event move on a name whose last print moved +18.76% says the market is already braced for exactly the kind of revenue surprise described. The 5-day run-up of -0.38% shows no fresh downward drift into the event, i.e. no evidence positioning has been de-risked in the direction this finding would exploit.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A primary defense.gov contract text (the site returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so I could not verify it directly) confirming both a 2026-07-23 completion inside the quarter and a delivery-based rather than over-time revenue recognition, plus a sell-side note showing the P550 order absent from Q1 product-sales models, would take this to the 20s.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The first leg restates the sealed baseline. run_up_20d_pct = -26.73 is the single most public number about this name, and a claim that the shares are down is definitionally in the price. The sector-wide framing is also published -- 24/7 Wall St. ran the same drone-complex slide story on 2026-08-18 as well as the cited 2026-08-24 piece. Worse, the finding's central assertion that there is 'no company announcement, contract award, earnings release, regulatory action, or analyst rating change' is contradicted by the record: AVAV carries a company-specific overhang from the SCAR stop-work of 2026-01-20 (a single-day -15.77% decline), the Space Force reopening SCAR to competition in March, a two-notch Raymond James cut to Underperform on 2026-03-02, and a securities class action whose lead-plaintiff notices were re-syndicated through the summer -- Quiver headlined AVAV sliding specifically on those notices, and 24/7 Wall St.'s own 2026-08-18 piece is titled 'Red Cat, Ondas Flat While AeroVironment Tumbles', which is the opposite of undifferentiated sector beta. The second leg is structural and disclosed: the 40/30/30 BlueHalo lock-up release schedule (2026-05-01, 2026-11-01, 2027-05-01) has been in the merger prospectus and the 424B3/424B5 filings since early 2025. The 40% tranche came free four months ago and is fully absorbed; the 30% tranche is due 2026-11-01, seven weeks after this print, so it cannot move tonight's tape except as a known calendar item.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: This claim is the baseline. The -26.73% twenty-day drawdown is a computed field of the sealed file, and the 1,248,947-share ADV the finding divides by is another. Restating two baseline fields and calling the quotient 5.6 days of supply adds no information the scorer does not already have from -run_up_20d_pct, which is itself the free control this stage has not yet beaten. The one place the baseline actively contradicts the finding's implied direction is the skew: if the market believed a 6.97M-share overhang were the live risk into the print, 25-delta puts would be bid; they are 15.51 vol points cheaper than calls. The flat 5-day run-up (-0.38%) also says the unwind stopped a week ago.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the 2026-11-01 tranche is being pre-hedged or shopped now -- a block-trade filing, a 144 notice, or a borrow-rate spike dated inside September -- would pull the overhang into this print's window and drop this to the 30s.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every factual component of this is in the wire copy, and the price reaction it describes is the baseline. The E-HEL award was announced by AeroVironment itself on 2026-09-02 and covered the same day and next by DefenseScoop, Breaking Defense, Defense News and Seeking Alpha, all of which characterised it as a multiyear production contract for 'dozens' of LOCUST X3 systems -- the multiyear, ceiling-not-booked-revenue framing the finding presents as its insight is in the primary coverage. The fiscal arithmetic is not a discovery either: AeroVironment's fiscal year ends 30 April, the quarter reported tonight closed 2026-08-01, and an award dated 2026-09-02 is trivially outside it for anyone who knows the fiscal calendar. The first international LOCUST order of more than $50 million was press-released by the company on 2026-09-08 and picked up by Defense Daily, defence-blog and securities.io within hours; it is one session old and equally outside the quarter. And the fade is observable rather than inferred: run_up_5d_pct is -0.38%, so the shares sit flat against the 2026-09-02 close, having produced no follow-through from either announcement. A finding whose evidence is that the market did not stay excited is a finding agreeing with the market. The one genuinely obscure element is the January Army draft solicitation seeking up to 24 systems over five years, which sizes the ceiling against realistic annual deliveries; that detail is not in the mainstream coverage and is worth something, but it is a valuation argument about FY28-FY30, not about tonight's reaction.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company press release on the $464.8M E-HEL selection, describing a multiyear production contract for LOCUST X3 systems.
The finding's own cited source, published the day of the award.
Independently reports the award as the Army's first laser production contract with a $465M value and a $30M Albuquerque capacity investment.
Frames it explicitly as a multiyear production award, i.e. spread across years rather than booked at once.
Company press release announcing the first international LOCUST order valued at more than $50M, one session before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: This is a bearish claim and it agrees with the tape while contradicting the option market. The tape supports it: run_up_5d_pct of -0.38% against a -26.73% twenty-day drawdown says the 09-02 and 09-08 announcements bought no net upside, exactly as the finding asserts. The skew cuts the other way: at -15.51 vol points the market is paying up for calls into the print, which is hard to reconcile with a market that has already written off the laser franchise as spent. On this name, then, a bearish claim is trading against the priced direction lean -- but it is doing so with material that is entirely published, so the disagreement is one of interpretation, not of information. Note the prior print moved +18.76%, so the market has recent evidence that this name can gap up on guidance regardless of what the awards contributed to the closed quarter.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A sell-side or buy-side note dated in the last week that models E-HEL revenue into FY27 guidance at a rate the January draft solicitation cannot support -- i.e. evidence that consensus has actually over-extrapolated the ceiling -- would make the gap real and take this to the 30s.

interactions: Three real overlaps. (1) #0 and #2 are mirror images of the same arithmetic: both turn entirely on which side of the 2026-08-01 fiscal quarter end a contract award falls, one arguing the P550 order lands inside it and the other that E-HEL and the international LOCUST order fall outside. They cannot both be independent evidence about tonight; they are one fiscal-calendar observation applied twice, and a scorer that counts both is counting the same insight in opposite directions. (2) #1 and #2 both rest on the same observed price action -- #1 on the -26.7% twenty-day drawdown and #2 on the faded 09-02 pop -- and both of those are the sealed baseline's run_up_20d_pct and run_up_5d_pct fields, not independent research. Crediting both double-counts the tape, and the tape is already the stage's free control. (3) #0's consensus figures and #2's award dating both come out of the same 2026-09-02/09-03 press cycle (the Zacks key-metrics syndication and the E-HEL coverage), so their apparent independence is a function of two different outlets, not two different facts. Separately, #1 contains an internal contradiction with the record rather than with another finding: its cited source asserts no company-specific news, while the same outlet six days earlier headlined AVAV tumbling while its drone peers were flat.
